title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Falls 14.0% on Reports of SEC Probe (Nov 20)
summary: Nvidia stock (NVDA) fell 14.01% to $125.53 on Nov. 20 after a Reuters report that the SEC is probing its accounting, amid a broad chip sell-off.
body_markdown:
The report landed a day after California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia on Thursday, November 19, the outlet reported. "My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips," Bonta said, adding that his office is also examining whether the company misled investors and the public about that risk.


Both inquiries follow[the CEO transition](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-nvda-stock-news-november-20-2026/) . According to[Nvidia's November 12 release](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-ceo-transition) , Huang resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress agreed to serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent chief executive, considering internal and external candidates.


The selling also reached well beyond Nvidia.[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-friday-november-19-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-anthropic-nvidia-141644188.html) reported that semiconductor stocks led an AI trade sell-off on Friday as selling pressure continued across tech after[Anthropic's public debut](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-prices-83-raises-81-billion/) on Thursday, and described the week as Nvidia's worst since October 2008.


## NVDA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Nvidia's latest[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) , released November 17, showed revenue up 103% year over year to $115.8 billion and net income up 105% to $65.3 billion, The Motley Fool reported.
- Nvidia's board said in its November 12 release that it expects the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption, with Kress also staying on as CFO.


### Risks


- Regulatory scrutiny is rising on two fronts, the reported SEC accounting probe and the California subpoena. The Motley Fool wrote that these regulatory and legal issues are leading more investors to question whether Nvidia's growth will continue.
- Nvidia has not yet named a permanent CEO, and the board's search covers both internal and external candidates.
- Chip stocks are falling together: AMD, Broadcom and Micron each lost more than 12% in the same session, which Yahoo Finance said was led lower by semiconductors.


The next dated event is a government deadline: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said Nvidia must tell the Trump administration by November 25 whether it set up shell companies to evade export controls, according to a separate[Motley Fool report](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/u-treasury-secretary-scott-bessent-210804381.html) .
